supporting_observations.claim: At 13:38:45 and 13:39:31 UTC, the domain controller issued Kerberos service tickets for the WS-MLOPEZ-01$ machine account to FILE-HD-01, with requests originating from WS-MLOPEZ-01. These records do not identify a PowerShell process or establish what prompted the requests.

At 13:44:40 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 used the proxy to tunnel to download.windowsupdate.com with a Windows Update Agent user agent; the tunnel transferred about 38.8 MB from the server to the client. This is consistent with update activity but does not establish that the reported PowerShell window initiated it.

The supplied process-creation records show a short-lived conhost.exe process at 14:12:25 UTC, running as SYSTEM with csrss.exe as its parent; the records do not identify it as PowerShell, and it is well after the reported 13:40 event.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include a PowerShell or pwsh process-creation event, command line, script-block log, or console event tied to the reported 13:40 UTC window.
Network and authentication records identify connections and accounts but do not attribute the relevant activity to a user-launched process.
The Windows Update proxy record is several minutes after the reported time and does not identify what initiated the download.
claims_not_established: Whether a PowerShell window actually appeared on WS-MLOPEZ-01 at about 13:40 UTC.
Whether any PowerShell activity was authorized patching, other legitimate administration, or malicious execution.
Whether the FILE-HD-01 Kerberos tickets near the reported time relate to the reported window.
additional_evidence_needed: Endpoint EDR or Windows process-creation telemetry for WS-MLOPEZ-01 around 13:40 UTC, including parent process, user, command line, and process start and end times.
PowerShell Operational logs, especially events 4103 and 4104, and any available console or terminal-session telemetry for the same period.
Windows Update and scheduled-task logs to determine what initiated the 13:44 download.
Administrative workstation and FILE-HD-01 share-access records to check whether the documented patching workflow was used.
unrelated_findings: Google Drive File Stream started under maria.lopez at 14:11 UTC and contacted dl.google.com. Google Drive is not listed among approved services; refer for separate review, without treating it as evidence about the reported PowerShell window. (T024-00278, T024-00280, T024-00281, T024-00282)

At 14:11–14:12 UTC, svchost.exe accessed lsass.exe with the recorded GrantedAccess values. The records do not identify the service or establish malicious intent; review separately from the alert. (T024-00283, T024-00284, T024-00289)

At 13:57 UTC, FILE-HD-01 initiated a connection to WS-MLOPEZ-01 on TCP port 135. The records do not establish the purpose or outcome; review separately from the reported 13:40 activity. (T024-00169, T024-00170)
